# Decisions (ADR log) — Alpha Detective

One line per decision. Date · decision · why. Details live in CONTRACTS.md (v1.2), review files, and BUILD_LOG.md.

- 2026-08-25 · Provider = Google Gemini free tier with keyless "none" fallback; no paid APIs anywhere · Sam's constraint; app must demo at $0.
- 2026-08-25 · Frontend = Next.js 16, JavaScript only, App Router + Tailwind; no UI kit · Sam's explicit stack choice.
- 2026-08-25 · Hybrid retrieval = Chroma dense (cosine) + BM25 → RRF (num_queries=1) → flashrank rerank (optional at runtime) · spec §6.5; num_queries=1 protects free-tier quota.
- 2026-08-25 · Structural pre-LLM no-answer guardrail (entity-presence, period-presence with quarter expansion, cross-doc exclusive-topic) — ratified r2 · literal BM25-floor sketch provably failed the unanswerable/scoping gates; frozen constants kept.
- 2026-08-25 · Citation snippets = question-relevant ≤300-char window (word-boundary, ellipsis), not chunk head — ratified r2 · required by the expect_substring-in-snippet accuracy gate.
- 2026-08-25 · Corruption fail-loud exit codes: 1 via `python -m app.main`, 3 under uvicorn CLI — ratified r2 · uvicorn owns its exit code; both documented.
- 2026-08-25 · Query `doc_ids` validation: non-string → 400 `bad_request`; malformed/unknown UUID → 404 `not_found` · uniform with DELETE semantics.
- 2026-08-25 · Health reports the reranker's *effective* state (`rerank:"off"` when flashrank init fails, config unchanged) · truthful ops signal.
- 2026-08-25 · Failed/duplicate uploads persist nothing — committed-flag cleanup rmtrees `uploads/{doc_id}/` on any non-committed exit · security M1 (disk-fill DoS + spec §1.3).
- 2026-08-25 · Anti-citation-forgery: bracketed `[n]` tokens inside source text are neutralized to `⟦n⟧` in the LLM context only (snippets untouched); deeper cited-claim↔source verification consciously deferred as accepted defense-in-depth · extractive default is immune; generative path keeps rule + range validation.
- 2026-08-25 · 405 responses use envelope code `not_found` (status 405) · contract's error-code table defines no `method_not_allowed`.
- 2026-08-25 · No file-download/static route exists at all; uploads are write-only storage · smaller attack surface.
- 2026-08-25 · Design: file-type chips stay neutral; red/green/amber reserved exclusively for status semantics · avoids "PDF=error" misreads (design round 2).
- 2026-08-25 · Canvas artifact URL is stable across design rounds (round-2-density republished in place) · Sam's review link must not rot.
- 2026-08-26 · `.env` values are de-commented before validation and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is dropped when implausible (leading `#`, whitespace, `#`, non-ASCII/non-printable) with one value-free warning — ratified r3 · python-dotenv keeps the comment as the value when the value is empty, so the shipped `.env.example` produced a 76-char "key" that reached an HTTP auth header and killed startup with a misleading "check the API key and network" error.
- 2026-08-26 · `PROVIDER=auto` is best-effort: any provider-init or model-resolution failure logs its cause once and boots retrieval-only (`provider:"none"`); explicit `PROVIDER=gemini` keeps the fail-loud `SystemExit(1)` — ratified r3 · `auto` means "figure it out" and keyless mode is fully supported; an operator who names a provider explicitly wants to hear it fail.
- 2026-08-26 · Retrieval inspector: `POST /api/query` gains `explain:true` returning a `pipeline` object built ONLY from data the pipeline already computed — zero extra LLM calls, zero extra embedding calls, never a second pass — ratified r3 · free-tier frugality, and an inspector that re-runs retrieval would be inspecting a different query than the one answered.
- 2026-08-26 · Stage recorders wrap the dense/sparse retrievers on EVERY query; only serialization is conditional on `explain` — ratified r3 · identical executed path in both modes is the only way to guarantee explain can never move a rank; QA gate asserts `citations` are identical with explain on/off.
- 2026-08-26 · A pipeline stage appears iff it actually ran: `dense` omitted entirely when keyless, `rerank` omitted entirely when rerank is off; `fusion` always present with `method:"rrf"` (gemini) or `"passthrough"` (keyless) — ratified r3 · `rerank.before_rank` needs a stable candidate-pool anchor and the keyless BM25 pool (12) is wider than the bm25 display cap (8).
- 2026-08-26 · Guardrail `checks` reports only the checks actually evaluated (short-circuit order preserved, unevaluated ones omitted, values stay exactly `pass`/`fail`) — ratified r3 · the object must never lie and must never force extra computation to fill itself.
- 2026-08-26 · Any chunk-metadata key added from v1.2 onward (`has_table`, `sheet`, `slide`) MUST be in both `excluded_embed_metadata_keys` and `excluded_llm_metadata_keys`, and the four v1.1 keys keep their names/values/insertion order — ratified r3 · BM25Retriever tokenizes `get_content(MetadataMode.EMBED)`, so an unexcluded key silently shifts sparse scores and puts the 100% eval gate at risk (dense is unaffected, which is what makes the trap easy to miss).
- 2026-08-26 · `parse_file`/`chunk_pages` keep their v1.1 2-tuple signatures as a de-facto test seam; the richer `parse_document`/`Block`/`ParsedDoc` live alongside and `chunk_pages` accepts either shape — ratified r3 · 101 green tests call these directly; compatibility beats elegance.
- 2026-08-26 · Per-doc `tables` count is recorded once at ingest into the manifest and echoed by upload/list (plus `totals.tables`); a v1.1 entry with no `tables` key reads as 0 with no migration and no manifest rewrite — ratified r3 · same store-consistency law as `pages`/`chunks`, and rewriting a healthy store at boot is the "silent rebuild" §3.4 bans.
- 2026-08-26 · `has_table` is block-level inheritance, not char-exact — ratified r3 · char-exactness would need sentinel text inside chunks and sentinels change BM25 tokens.
- 2026-08-26 · New ingest formats `.xlsx .pptx .html/.htm .json` with named extraction caps (`OOXML_MAX_ENTRIES/UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES/COMPRESSION_RATIO`, `XLSX_MAX_SHEETS/CELLS`, `PPTX_MAX_SLIDES/TABLE_CELLS`, `HTML_MAX_TEXT_CHARS`, `JSON_MAX_DEPTH/NODES`); exceeding a cap is a clean per-file error with HTTP 200, never a crash — ratified r3 · zip bombs and depth bombs are the realistic attack on new parsers, and per-file failure is the semantics upload already has.
- 2026-08-26 · HTML is tag-stripped to inert text with `<script>`/`<style>`/comments dropped and tables NOT parsed (`tables:0`); JSON is flattened iteratively with an explicit stack — ratified r3 · inert text is the security posture, and counted depth never becomes recursed depth.
- 2026-08-26 · Scanned/image-only PDFs keep failing with `no extractable text`; no OCR dependency in v1.2 — ratified r3 · OCR is weight and cost for a $0 free-tier deploy.
- 2026-08-26 · §5 env matrix expands 5 → 12 vars (`PORT`, `CORS_ORIGINS`, `ACCESS_CODE`, `DAILY_LLM_BUDGET`, `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`, `MAX_DOCUMENTS`, `AUTO_SEED`) — ratified r3 · deployment needs port/origin/gate/spend/throttle/cap/seed knobs; everything else stays a code constant and further additions need architect ratification.
- 2026-08-26 · New envelope code `unauthorized` (401) for the `ACCESS_CODE` gate — the enum goes 6 → 7 and no further; the per-IP throttle deliberately reuses `rate_limited` (429) — ratified r3 · a truthful code for auth, and one 429 path for the frontend.
- 2026-08-26 · `ACCESS_CODE` gates every `/api` route except `GET /api/health`, compared with `hmac.compare_digest`, never logged; it is a quota gate, not a security boundary — ratified r3 · health must answer before a code is entered (poll + container probe), and the browser necessarily holds the code, so calling it security would be a lie; `GOOGLE_API_KEY` stays server-side only.
- 2026-08-26 · Rate limit ~10/min per IP applies only to `POST /api/query`, `POST /api/documents`, `DELETE /api/documents/{id}`; GET routes are exempt and the tracked-IP table is bounded at 4096 with eviction — ratified r3 · `useHealth` polls every 10s (6/min) so throttling reads would lock an honest user out of their own UI, and an unbounded IP table is itself a memory DoS.
- 2026-08-26 · `DAILY_LLM_BUDGET` (default 200/UTC day, counter persisted at `storage/llm_budget.json`, derived data) degrades an over-budget query to extractive with `degraded_reason:"daily_budget"` and an amber note; retrieval never stops and reservations are never refunded — ratified r3 · availability beats generation, and a refund path invites double-spend.
- 2026-08-26 · Uvicorn binds `0.0.0.0` iff `PORT` is present in the environment, else `127.0.0.1` — ratified r3 · Render dictates the port; local dev must not start exposing itself to the LAN as a side effect of deployment support.
- 2026-08-26 · `AUTO_SEED=on` ingests `backend/sample_data/` through the normal ingest path (same lock, keyless-safe, logged) when the manifest is empty at startup, and never blocks or fails boot — ratified r3 · Render's free-tier disk is ephemeral, and a blank demo after every redeploy is worse than a seeded one.
- 2026-08-26 · `RERANK=off` is the documented posture for Render's 512MB free tier — ratified r3 · the cross-encoder + ONNX runtime is the largest resident allocation and the realistic OOM cause; the eval gate is 100% with rerank on AND off, and health reports the effective state truthfully.
- 2026-08-26 · Frontend v1.2 surface is additive only: `getDocumentChunks`, `postQuery({explain})`, `X-Access-Code` from `NEXT_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CODE` or localStorage, `BACKEND_ORIGIN` for the rewrite, 429 banner text now uses the server envelope message, and an optional `PipelineInspector` — no new design tokens; JS-only unchanged — ratified r3 · deployment and the inspector must not become a visual redesign; layout calls stay with design-lead on the approved canvas.
- 2026-08-26 · Frontend access code is held **in memory only** (module-scope state in `lib/api.js`, dies with the tab) — never `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/cookie; `NEXT_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CODE` may seed it at build time and a typed code overrides it — ratified r3, supersedes the localStorage line in the v1.2 CONTRACTS draft · Sam's standing instruction, and a persisted code survives tab close and is readable by any script on the origin, so one XSS or bad dependency exfiltrates it permanently; memory-only removes the persisted-read path and `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined into the public bundle so it is a demo convenience, never a secret (GOOGLE_API_KEY stays server-side only).
- 2026-08-26 · Middleware ordering is specified in REQUEST order — CORS → body-size → access-code → throttle → router (add order in `create_app` is its reverse) — and a 401 never consumes a throttle slot — ratified r3, fixes a self-contradiction between the v1.2 §2 list (add order) and §1.10 · if rejected requests counted, an attacker without the access code could spoof `X-Forwarded-For` and exhaust a victim IP's quota, locking out a legitimate user.
- 2026-08-26 · `PPTX_MAX_TABLE_CELLS` is a **soft** cap (truncate table serialization, log once, keep indexing the deck, no per-file error, no error string) while every other extraction cap stays hard — ratified r3 · the hard caps guard unbounded work where partial output is worthless; a table-heavy deck is a legitimate document whose slide text still has value, so degrading beats rejecting.
- 2026-08-26 · `top_k` is a strict int: `"6"` and `6.0` now return 400 `bad_request` where v1.1 silently coerced them — ratified r3 · a retrieval depth arriving as a string or float is a caller bug, and silent coercion hides it; no in-tree call site sends `top_k`, so the tightening ships with zero breakage.
- 2026-08-26 · Inspector `k` means the depth the stage ACTUALLY operated at in every stage (so keyless rerank-off fusion reports `top_k`, not the `FUSION_POOL` constant), and stage scores are snapshotted at capture time — ratified r3 · `rerank_nodes` mutates `NodeWithScore.score` in place, and an observability view that echoes a configured constant or a later-mutated score is worse than no view at all.
- 2026-08-26 · `explain: null` behaves exactly as absent (200, no `pipeline` key) while every other non-bool — `"true"`, `1`, `[]` — is 400 `bad_request`; field is a strict `bool | None = False` — ratified r3, §1.6 and §1.9 now state the identical rule · clients routinely serialize an unset optional as `null`, and that is "no value", not a wrong value; truthiness is never inferred from strings or numbers.
- 2026-08-26 · An empty `X-Access-Code` header counts as PRESENT and yields `Invalid access code`, with no emptiness special-case before `hmac.compare_digest`; the two 401 messages stay distinguishable but uninformative and never reveal whether a code is configured — ratified r3 · the client sent the header and got it wrong, and an early `if not provided` branch is exactly the kind of shortcut that erodes constant-time comparison.
- 2026-08-26 · `RERANK_MODEL_DIR` stays OUT of the frozen path seams as the sole sanctioned exception to "tests never touch real backend/storage", conditioned on it holding no test-visible state, on promotion to a seam before anything authoritative is ever written there, and on a QA guard asserting the real storage dir contains nothing but `models/` after a run — ratified r3, written into new §3.6 · the directory is a read-only third-party model download that is non-authoritative and rebuildable, and redirecting it would re-download a cross-encoder every run, making the suite slow, network-dependent and broken offline for zero isolation benefit.
- 2026-08-26 · Rate-limit client identity is the socket peer by default, or `xff[-TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS]` (last hop on Render's single proxy) when trusted proxies are declared; the v1.2 "first hop of X-Forwarded-For" rule is WITHDRAWN as a contract defect — ratified r3, new `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` env var (default 0, Render 1), §5 goes 12 → 13 vars · security-engineer reproduced both halves live — total bypass by rotating spoofed values, and victim targeting via `XFF: <victim>, <attacker>` burning the victim's bucket — i.e. the contract specified the exact capability its own no-slot-on-401 rationale existed to deny; only the rightmost N hops are proxy-written and unforgeable.
- 2026-08-26 · The throttle is a quota rail, not an authentication boundary — it does not identify users, does not survive NAT or a proxy pool, and nothing may be built assuming it does — ratified r3 · stated in §1.10 so its guarantees are never over-read.
- 2026-08-26 · New format-agnostic `MAX_EXTRACTED_TEXT_CHARS = 5_000_000`, enforced incrementally on accumulated extracted text during parsing for ALL formats, hard cap, frozen error `extracted text too large (cap: {MAX_EXTRACTED_TEXT_CHARS} characters)`; `HTML_MAX_TEXT_CHARS` folded into it and removed as a special case (same value, identical HTML behavior); `OOXML_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES` lowered 200 MiB → 100 MiB — ratified r3 · a 2.6 MB `.docx` at compression ratio 68 passed all three archive caps and parsed to 983 MB / 3.4 GB of nodes on a 512 MB tier, because the frozen caps guarded the archive and nothing guarded extracted text volume; a post-hoc check would BE the OOM, so the accumulator must abort mid-parse.
- 2026-08-26 · Deliberate v1.1 tightening: any document extracting to more than 5,000,000 characters is now rejected per-file where v1.1 indexed it — ratified r3 · 5 M characters is already ~2,800 chunks, an embedding bill that exhausts the free tier on a single upload; documented rather than silent.
- 2026-08-26 · v1.2 ships NO tenancy: the corpus is single-tenant and shared, any code-holder can delete any document, `MAX_DOCUMENTS` is a grief-able shared ceiling, and `AUTO_SEED` only re-seeds on a startup with an empty manifest; per-visitor isolation is explicitly out of scope and would be a contract change, not a patch — ratified r3, stated in §1.10 and §5.1 · the access code was being over-read as "the answer to abuse", and the honest scope of the demo deployment belongs in writing.
- 2026-08-26 · `GET /api/documents/{id}/chunks` stays deliberately uncapped and unthrottled; the §1.8 `len(chunks) == manifest chunks` invariant is absolute and `MAX_EXTRACTED_TEXT_CHARS` is the real bound (~2,800 chunks / under ~1 MB worst case, down from ~62,500) — ratified r3, security m5, with a tripwire to revisit via an explicit `truncated` field (never via throttling the route) if that cap is ever raised · a silently truncated list would make two numbers that must agree disagree, which is the store-consistency bug class §3 exists to prevent, and throttling a lazy on-expand UI read would carve the GET exemption that keeps honest users from locking themselves out.
